pr_title: adds TLS signature algorithms list feature
pr_body:
Fixes #24535 

This works with providers that support the "TLS-SIGALG" [capability](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man7/provider-base.html).

This then begs the question whether this capability should be added to the built-in providers? As part of this PR or a separate one? Or would anyone prefer extending this PR with a hack to expose the current [sigalg_lookup_tbl](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/24535#issuecomment-2141426971)?
pr_comments:
I think it should list the built-in sig algs as well (somehow separated from the provider ones). It is similar to the `
openssl list -cipher-algorithms` command.

> I think it should list the built-in sig algs as well (somehow separated from the provider ones). It is similar to the ` openssl list -cipher-algorithms` command.

I'd agree. The question is how it should do that. I see two options:
1) Expose [sigalg_lookup_table](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/d8def79838cd0d5e7c21d217aa26edb5229f0ab4/ssl/t1_lib.c#L1383) (as mentioned by @mattcaswell ) or
2) Expose built-in providers' sigalgs via capabilities (sounds like having a long-term benefit -- but IMO warrants a separate PR).

Any preferences or alternatives?

This PR looks good.

I agree there are long term benefits in having the built-in sigalgs exposed via the standard providers as a capability. We perhaps should have done so from the beginning. However this does bring the disadvantage that it only works for those providers where we have made this change. The most obvious case where this would not be true is if someone is using a validated version of the fips provider from an older release (e.g. 3.0.9) with a more recent version of OpenSSL. We could perhaps cover that via documentation (e.g. basically say that it may not correctly report sigalgs for older providers)

> We perhaps should have done so from the beginning. 

Mea culpa; I just didn't think about the built-in providers when adding provider-loaded TLS sigalgs (they worked :). Speaks for back-porting this as well as a "TLS-SIGALG" capabilities enhancement PR for the built-in providers, though.

> The most obvious case where this would not be true is if someone is using a validated version of the fips provider from an older release (e.g. 3.0.9) with a more recent version of OpenSSL.

Well, such FIPS provider would (could! should?) not support provider-loaded sigalgs anyway, so that'd be no problem, right? Or would the FIPS-provider-3.0.9-based TLS sigalg work even though it'd not be reported ("courtesy" `sigalg_lookup_tbl`?). If so (?) that'd speak for exposing `sigalg_lookup_tbl` to this new `list` app command.

> Well, such FIPS provider would (could! should?) not support provider-loaded sigalgs anyway, so that'd be no problem, right? Or would the FIPS-provider-3.0.9-based TLS sigalg work even though it'd not be reported ("courtesy" sigalg_lookup_tbl?). If so (?) that'd speak for exposing sigalg_lookup_tbl to this new list app command.

Right - a 3.0.9 based FIPS provider should "just work" for TLS because the sigalg_lookup_tbl provides all the necessary codepoints - but the new list feature would not work with it because it doesn't have the "TLS-SIGALG" capability. This was my point above about possibly handling this via the list app documentation, i.e. "we could just say in the docs: don't expect this to work for old providers"

We could maybe do both (1) and (2), i.e. the motivation for (1) would be to ensure that the list command works no matter whether you are using an old provider or not. The motivation for (2) would be to get the long term benefits of having these providers declaring these things.
IMO we should do (1) as the first step. (2) can be done independently any time later.

(1) implemented in latest commit. A bit more complicated than I thought because `sigalg_lookup_tbl` didn't contain all algorithm names; I found them in a "mirror data structure" https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/42230f294ae97cbd50052038499e091d0060ba8e/ssl/t1_trce.c#L570 though: Hoping this approach is OK.

Hmm -- running into all kind of "style" mistakes (incl. in code I didn't change): Is there a place where I could read up on this and learn how to run & fix this (new?) test locally instead of via "CI-debugging"? Thanks in advance for a pointer!

If you rebase on top of master, many should be resolved.  Additionally you may want to pull in this commit
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24861/commits/cdca0cd04b6761ece515796b7f19d536f8a8a225

As it fixes the REND problems that arise when git diff sometimes doesn't produce a proper git end line count

For now we can waive the style issues by setting the style:waived label, but please try to parse out any relevant style issues relevant to your patch set

Thanks for this quick reaction andf guidance, @nhorman !

> Please try to parse out any relevant style issues relevant to your patch set

Would do -- but how do I trigger local style testing? With the label now set I don't see the CI error messages any more...

Another question pertaining to a (presumably ssl-lib local) symbol I introduced to expose t1_trce functionality to t1_lib: This seems to work for most setups, but not for two CI jobs: Any idea what I'd need to change there? Do I need to also declare `ssl_get_sigalg_name` as a public symbol now?

No worries.  If you examine the ci job, you'll see that if you click the triangle next to the commit range error report, the style errors are still actually reported, the setting of the style:waived flag just forces the ci check to return successfully.  So you can still review them at will.

As for your symbol question, I'm not sure.  I'll need to look at the PR.to tell more (in the car atm), but what you're describing sounds like a static vs dynamic issue.  If you create a symbol and don't export it, it doesn't show up in the dao file, but if you link statically, you can still resolve the symbol because you have visibility on all symbols in the libssl.a and libcrypro.a files

Does that sound like what might be going on?

> So you can still review them at will.

Thanks for the hint: Indeed all code lines changed by the PR are now accepted, so I consider this dealt with.

> if you link statically, you can still resolve the symbol because you have visibility on all symbols in the libssl.a and libcrypro.a files
> Does that sound like what might be going on?

Nope, to the contrary: The problematic one is indeed a config ("minimal") that generates .a files. All .so configs pass. Together with a Windows job it's the only one complaining about a (new) symbol that is (within) "ssl_local". I'm anyway not happy about this as this is just a workaround for missing algorithm names in `sigalg_lookup_tbl`: I'd much rather change that table to contain the names instead but don't know whether this (`lu->name == NULL` for some sigalgs) is somehow intentional (?).
Just noticed the tags assigned: Any chance this can be considered for back-porting to OpenSSL 3.2 as this aligns with the provider-based TLS signing introduced in that release?
OTC: **back port through to 3.2 or not?**

> Nope, to the contrary: The problematic one is indeed a config ("minimal") that generates .a files. All .so configs pass. Together with a Windows job it's the only one complaining about a (new) symbol that is (within) "ssl_local". I'm anyway not happy about this as this is just a workaround for missing algorithm names in `sigalg_lookup_tbl`: I'd much rather change that table to contain the names instead but don't know whether this (`lu->name == NULL` for some sigalgs) is somehow intentional (?).

You would have to factorize the function out of t1_trce.c as that is not built in builds disabling the SSL trace support. But can't SSL_group_to_name() be used to convert  a group id to name?

> But can't SSL_group_to_name() be used to convert a group id to name?

Thanks for that suggestion; this call seems to require an SSL connection (object), though. Is your idea to create a "dummy" SSL object without real connection for this purpose? OK, let me try this...

> But can't SSL_group_to_name() be used to convert a group id to name?

Oops -- group_to_name won't resolve sig alg names.

> You would have to factorize the function out of t1_trce.c as that is not built in builds disabling the SSL trace support.

Back to that option. OK to move this function (and the related data structs) to t1_lib then?

On third thought: Instead of introducing another function wouldn't it be much cleaner to replace the few NULL `name` entries in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/01753c09bbfdffcefd555b4c21e50e68af346129/ssl/t1_lib.c#L1383-L1483 with the names properly listed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/01753c09bbfdffcefd555b4c21e50e68af346129/ssl/t1_trce.c#L570-L602, e.g., by way of #defines's. Does anything speak against this?

> > But can't SSL_group_to_name() be used to convert a group id to name?
> 
> Oops -- group_to_name won't resolve sig alg names.

Ouch, I'm sorry, not sure how I confused these two. :grinning:

> On third thought: Instead of introducing another function wouldn't it be much cleaner to replace the few NULL `name` entries in
> 
> https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/01753c09bbfdffcefd555b4c21e50e68af346129/ssl/t1_lib.c#L1383-L1483
> with the names properly listed in
> 
> https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/01753c09bbfdffcefd555b4c21e50e68af346129/ssl/t1_trce.c#L570-L602
> , e.g., by way of #defines's. Does anything speak against this?

Adding the name there will make it possible to use the name in the SignatureAlgorithms config setting. However I do not see any problem with that. @mattcaswell any idea why are some of these names NULL?

> why are some of these names NULL?

Latest commit changes this and streamlines use of these names within t1_lib and t1_trce, doing away with the need for a helper function.

Note: [Here's](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a753547eefc9739f341824a0cb0642afe7a06fcc/apps/lib/s_cb.c#L753) another duplication of these names: Worthwhile streamlining, too? Same or separate PR?

> OTC: **back port through to 3.2 or not?**

**OTC: This is a new feature. There is no compelling reason to justify backporting it to 3.2 in exception of the stable branch policy.**

> > OTC: **back port through to 3.2 or not?**
> 
> **OTC: This is a new feature. There is no compelling reason to justify backporting it to 3.2 in exception of the stable branch policy.**

ACK. Rebased & ready for review.

> Perhaps a CHANGES.md entry is appropriate for this new feature?

Not entirely sure as it's a rather small feature. Added in latest commit -- feel free to keep/amend/remove as you see fit.

> Approved, but please consider the comment above from @Sashan

Considered (&commented, see above) but do not think this is something this PR can/should resolve.

issue_context.title: Retrieve the names of available signature algorithms in the age of providers
issue_context.body:
As suggested in the discussion below, this is to propose a new openssl app, or extension to an existing app like `list` or an external script facilitating the retrieval of currently available signature algorithms in a form suitable for consumption by the openssl config file. ### Discussed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/discussions/24522
Originally posted by **baentsch** May 29, 2024 The [provider mechanism](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.3/man7/provider.html) allows (potentially many) different signature algorithms to be accessible to the `openssl` TLS logic. The [openssl config](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man3/SSL_CONF_cmd.html) mechanism allows the ones actually active to be configured/limited, e.g., to [work around server problems with too many active signature algorithms](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/issues/399). The question now is: Is there a mechanism by which the unwary user can retrieve a list of all permitted values to the "SignatureAlgorithms" config parameter, e.g., along the lines of `openssl list -signature-algorithms` (which does take providers into account, but does not output "fully qualified" algorithm names for use by the configuration, e.g. and incl. hash algs)?
comments:
I'm not sure it's doable in general. E.g. when we have a 3rd-party provider providing a signature algorithm working together with some common hash algorithm taken from the default provider.

Probably a provider documentation + some testing against the current configuration file will be OK.

> I'm not sure it's doable in general. E.g. when we have a 3rd-party provider providing a signature algorithm working together with some common hash algorithm taken from the default provider.

Agreed. But should such providers not register a suitable name? But then again, as per [@levitte 's comment](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/discussions/24522#discussioncomment-9614021) providers only register the sigalg name, not the TLS one....
> 
> Probably a provider documentation + some testing against the current configuration file will be OK.

The [original problem](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider/issues/399#issuecomment-2111198167) by @mouse07410 would arguably not be solved that way as the use case there (if I got it right) encompasses more than one provider.

> s there a mechanism by which the unwary user can retrieve a list of all permitted values to the "SignatureAlgorithms" config parameter, e.g., along the lines of openssl list -signature-algorithms (which does take providers into account, but does not output "fully qualified" algorithm names for use by the configuration, e.g. and incl. hash algs)?

There is a *programmatic* mechanism to query all the available providers about TLS SignatureAlgorithms that they want to plug in. Providers adding new TLS SignatureAlgorithms do so via the `TLS-SIGALG` capability, which can be queried via the `OSSL_PROVIDER_get_capabilities()` function. Libssl does exactly this to query all providers, e.g. see:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9fcf57b45985336b04579dd317d0dc990a9c062b/ssl/t1_lib.c#L692-L733

The complication is that libssl adds the provider plugged-in sigalgs with its own hard-coded built-in list:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9fcf57b45985336b04579dd317d0dc990a9c062b/ssl/t1_lib.c#L1509-L1595

So the full list of TLS sigalgs are the combination of these two things.  The above code also checks the built-in list to confirm if it is actually usable from the available providers. Only available sigalgs from the combined list are actually usable by TLS applications.

So, it would be feasible to `extend` the list app with a way to query the capabilities of the providers to see what TLS sig-algs can be plugged in. But there is currently no mechanism to query which of the "built-in" TLS sig-algs are actually usable.

> So the full list of TLS sigalgs are the combination of these two things. 

Right. One actually would only have to traverse the list of all currently active `TLS_SIGALG_INFO` structs -- also delivering the hashes. Let me give that a try extending the `list` app...

> But there is currently no mechanism to query which of the "built-in" TLS sig-algs are actually usable.

Nevertheless it shows which ones _may_ be available (in `sigalg_lookup_tbl`), right? And that was the original ask: How does the unwary user learn about the names of all possibly configurable (TLS) "SignatureAlgorithms". Only question in my mind right now: Can the `list` app get access to `sigalg_lookup_tbl`?

> Can the list app get access to sigalg_lookup_tbl?

Unfortunately not - this is an internal global variable in libssl and is not exposed.

> > Can the list app get access to sigalg_lookup_tbl?
> 
> Unfortunately not - this is an internal global variable in libssl and is not exposed.

Hmm -- may I ask what you'd think about these two initial thoughts for ways how to deal with this then?
1) Would it be OK to consider adding an API to do so, e.g., by populating a (then also publicly accessible) TLS_SIGALG_INFO list from that struct? This would arguably be a sub-optimal solution as that'd perpetuate this "internal" mechanism, though. Sub-thought: There seems to be an "apps"-based subset of the information in `sigalg_lookup_tbl`, namely in [signature_tls13_scheme_list](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0285160ffa3b8c2b5491222243042593808298c4/apps/lib/s_cb.c#L753-L776): Would that be something that an app listing the "built-in" TLS sigalgs could sensibly use (and maybe extend to be completely in sync with `sigalg_lookup_tbl`)? But duplicating this information also feels wrong (brittle code if only one place gets changed).
2) What should happen if one queries the default provider just like a "normal" provider: Would that be a way to glean the same information as in `sigalg_lookup_tbl`? Or do I see it right that one first would have to enhance the "built-in" provider(s) to follow the [provider documentation](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man7/provider-base.html) concerning the "TLS-SIGALG" Capability (that I created, admittedly :)? This at first glance seems doable, mirroring the logic in [for TLS groups](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0285160ffa3b8c2b5491222243042593808298c4/providers/common/capabilities.c#L210-L221): Would this be worth while doing/a welcome enhancement in general and beyond this issue?

I believe the answer to question 1 is yes, its always ok to propose/consider a change like this.  I would encourage you to open a pull request.  We can't guarantee the outcome of course, as thats dependent on the review of the pr and issues that may be identified with it.  If you're not ready to invest the time in a full PR, I would encourage you to write a design document here first for an initial comment round to better determine its feasibility.

Each provider should "provide" a list of algorithms it supports (for use in `pkeyutl` and such),  **and** a list (subset) of algorithms it wants to export to TLS. If only one list is provided, it's used for both.

Any other attempt to approach this problem is likely to turn out more curbmersome and taxing than the one proposed above.
@mouse07410 @baentsch are either of you willing to compose a PR for this?  I'm happy to assign it to you as a community issue

I'm not - I've neither competence nor time for that. 

Not to mention that I think this whole approach is bad/barely-sustainable, and a simple added ability for each provider to report two algorithm sets would be an easier-implementable solution, suitable for both short-term and long-term.

> @mouse07410 @baentsch are either of you willing to compose a PR for this? I'm happy to assign it to you as a community issue

I can surely give this a try for all "documentation-supporting" providers (as per the suggestion by @mattcaswell , it would be a cut-copy-paste of the code I already did for the implementation of the "TLS-SIGALG" capability); for the built-ins, well, it'll take a (arguably separate) PR to add the "TLS-SIGALG" capability to default and FIPS provider. I'm still not entirely sure how to properly capture all digests the sigalgs may support...

A new provider side API (or APIs) might be the way to go here.

With a single new API, a provider could advertise all the sigalgs it supports in isolation.
Better might be multiple API that combine to handle the various different parts (in the TLS 1.2 world, I'm not sure how 1.3 would cope).

> A new provider side API (or APIs) might be the way to go here.

Something like "give me a colon-separated list of all (EVP|TLS) sigalg/hashalg combinations you support"? Would surely be more simple than querying capability sets...
I'm not sure I get how do you plan to use this API and why it's better than documentation

> I'm not sure I get how do you plan to use this API and why it's better than documentation

Partial answer to this was the reason for asking which API @paulidale and/or @mouse07410 had in mind (?). My thought was to use it with an extended version of the `list` app.

Another partial answer is that documentation is not solving the issue as well as code: Different provider (version(s)) will support different algorithm sets. Also, different `openssl` versions (particularly if configured with different built-in providers) will provide different algorithm sets. And lastly, the current documentation seems to be too difficult to understand for @mouse07410 -- and s/he never appeared to me to be not capable (incl. grasping documentation), so it'll be a harder problem for the "common Joe User" (to know which algs are available with a currently configured collection of binaries (openssl/libcrypto + providers)).

Ok, so what I'm reading here is that based on @paulidale comment, we have an idea for a provider api to accomplish this, and @baentsch is willing to take a shot at writing it.  Thank you @baentsch !

I'm assigning this as a community issue to you, please link your PR here when you have it available.

>  @baentsch is willing to take a shot at writing it.

That's a gross oversimplification :-) but OK. @paulidale : Could you please be more specific what (new?) API you had in mind? I'd otherwise proceed using the already defined ["sigalg-name" capability](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/doc/man7/provider-base.pod#tls-sigalg-capability) to extract (TLS) alg names for the `list` app (as basically proposed by @mattcaswell ) and augment that with extensions to the default&FIPS provider capabilities to get a complete list.
This has been implemented (in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24821) and thus can be closed.

I also think  `TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_256_gostr34112012_256_name` should be changed to `TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_256_gostr34112012_name` (there is one more extra 256).
Same goes to `TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_512_gostr34112012_512_name`.

thanks.

> Would it make sense to distinguish gostr34102012_*_intrinsic from gostr34102012_*_gostr34112012_*? We currently use gost2012_* for all of them.

Conceptually sure -- but this decision to label all "Gost's" the same [pre-dates this PR](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fd39d1c80cd5bd9cb5c64e3fc96102397e5e860f/ssl/t1_trce.c#L594-L597), so touching this seems risky as this name may be externally used/referenced. Who could comment on this mainly Gost-related question? @beldmit?

> I also think TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_256_gostr34112012_256_name should be changed to TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_256_gostr34112012_name

Sure -- we can do this. But we could also use "TLSEXT_SIGALG_gostr34102012_gostr34112012_256_name" instead with the logic that the presumed strength (256) trails the presumed base algorithm name. Again, unsure what suits better the Gost spirit (sorry, couldn't resist the pun :).

Oh, and this naming again has nothing really to do with this PR but is just following what is in the current "master":

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/fd39d1c80cd5bd9cb5c64e3fc96102397e5e860f/ssl/t1_trce.c#L594-L597
